paragraphs.source_zh: “长筱城灭亡之日就是德川氏灭亡之日。”家康的这句话，九八郎信以为真，不假思索就记在了心里。家康唯一的女儿龟姬就嫁到了这里，因此，他绝不会坐视不管。援军一定会赶来。

paragraphs.source_en: If the reinforcements still had not arrived when the moment came, and Nagashino Castle met the same fate as Takatenjin Castle… No, even then Kyūhachirō would bear Ieyasu no resentment. He had long since prepared himself for that possibility.

paragraphs.source_en: If the time truly came for Kamehime and him to perish together with the castle, he would show her that he could die smiling. At the very least, people must say of him that he had never sullied his father’s illustrious name. Of course, the pillar secretly sustaining him was in fact his victory in winning Kamehime’s love, though even he himself did not realize it. In that sense, Kamehime was the first enemy he had faced within this castle.

paragraphs.source_en: Anyone with human feelings would have trembled all over with rage. At that moment, Kyūhachirō was like a maddened tiger. He smiled and said, “Kamehime, do you hate me?”

paragraphs.source_en: “Your father said I was a capable man worthy of trust. That is why I think you and your father are utterly different.” With that, Kyūhachirō strode swiftly out.

paragraphs.source_en: Kamehime was so astonished that she could not utter a word. It might be said that this marked the beginning of the war between them. Kamehime boasted to the ladies of the inner chambers, “Even if I have to bite off my own tongue, I will never share his bed.”

paragraphs.source_en: Kyūhachirō, however, remained perfectly calm and unhurried. When evening came, he brought his guards to Kamehime’s quarters, ate his meal there as though it were the most natural thing in the world, and even stayed talking until late at night.

units.source_en: Kyūhachirō, however, remained perfectly calm and unhurried.

paragraphs.source_zh: 可是，九八郎却心平气和，不慌不忙。到了晚上，他带了侍卫来到龟姬的居室，竟然在此吃起饭来，甚至还聊到深夜。

paragraphs.source_en: “Are you still sulking?” Kyūhachirō remained unruffled. When his steady gaze met the flames of anger in Kamehime’s eyes, he roared with laughter and walked out.

paragraphs.source_en: As this went on, Kamehime began to worry: did he perhaps dislike women? Was she to spend her entire life with a man who could look straight through her as if she were not there? The very fact that Kamehime had begun to think this way meant she was about to lose the war.

paragraphs.source_en: The next evening, Kyūhachirō came smiling as usual, still behaving as though nothing had happened. Then he began speaking loudly and endlessly of military affairs—of Uesugi Kenshin Nyūdō of Echigo and this or that Oda commander. This time, after he had finished speaking, Kamehime approached him of her own accord.

paragraphs.source_zh: 第二天晚上，九八郎照样笑呵呵地来了，依然一副若无其事的样子，然后高声谈论一些军情，越后的上杉谦信入道如何啦，织田大将怎么样啦，说个没完。这次，龟姬等他谈完之后，主动去亲近他。

paragraphs.source_en: Kamehime intended to repay him in kind. To humiliate him, she would first draw close, then reject him cruelly and leave him mortified. Kyūhachirō, however, walked away with a grin. “Today is the anniversary of my grandfather’s death. Please show some respect.”

paragraphs.source_en: After Kyūhachirō rejected her, Kamehime, driven into a corner, commenced her second campaign. For Kamehime, to be rejected again would be an unbearable humiliation. She clung to him with coy reluctance, only to be deftly subdued by Kyūhachirō once more.

paragraphs.source_en: In his preparations for war, Kyūhachirō overlooked not even the smallest detail. Ever since repairs to the castle had begun, he had continually sent copies of the plans to Ieyasu for his inspection. Only through Kyūhachirō did Kamehime begin to understand what weighed on her father’s mind.

paragraphs.source_en: “If the castle should fall, I too shall remain here and share life and death with you.” Kamehime spoke with perfect clarity. She had already realized that her father might abandon both his daughter and son-in-law to their fate.
